description: Deliberately weld two incompatible voices into a hybrid where one supplies the body (cadence, vocabulary, characteristic moves) and the other supplies a register the first lacks (depth, precision, structural insight, ethical attention). The graft is visible and acknowledged, not seamless. The first voice acknowledges its insufficiency at the moment of graft; the second voice does what the first cannot. Example: Frazerian comparative narrative + Neoplatonic philosophical penetration — Frazer carries the prose, Proclus carries the depth. Use when the user invites a voice good for some things and bad for others, and the conversation needs both — when pure pastiche would be empty but pure exposition flat. Triggers on: hybrid invitations like 'Frazerian prose receiving Neoplatonic content'; requests combining 'write in X voice' with 'engage Y subject matter properly'; explicit invocations of 'graft', 'weld these voices', 'hybrid register'.
